citation.title: PyTOaCNN: Topology optimization using an adaptive convolutional neural network in Python
citation.version_coded: arXiv v1 (18 Apr 2024); full text used because version of record was not accessed

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The adaptive CNN generates designs resembling MATLAB topology-optimization outputs with small reported volume and objective errors.
claim.key_phrase: negligible performance and volume fraction errors
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No classical-to-ML speed-up factor is reported or derivable.
claim.alternatives: The abstract also says the trained model produces a design instantly; conclusion calls the approach expediting, without a timed classical comparison.

baseline.classical_method: Open-source MATLAB topology optimization codes (SIMP-based compliance problems; TOPress; TopX for bulk modulus)
baseline.implementation: MATLAB codes; author code appendix for CNN
baseline.ml_time: fraction of a second per design (Sec. 7.1.3); exact value not stated
baseline.training_time: not stated; 2000 epochs reported for several models (Sec. 7)
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; training sets of 95, 68, or 32 examples reported (Secs. 7.1.3-7.2)
baseline.quality_metric: volume fraction error and objective function error, plus visual topology comparison (Tables 1-7)
baseline.quality_gap: Table 7 shows volume/objective errors across tested volume fractions; e.g. varying errors by adaptive-layer size; no single overall gap.

R1.evidence: Abstract and Sec. 7 compare output quality; no matched-time speed comparison is reported.

R2.evidence: Secs. 7-8 provide no timing comparison against a classical baseline.

R3.evidence: Secs. 5 and 7-8 describe generated training data and instantaneous inference, but report neither data-generation cost nor elapsed training cost or break-even accounting.

R4.evidence: Sec. 7 and Tables 1-7 compare volume and objective errors with MATLAB targets, but no rate of disconnected, infeasible, or failed designs is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Different volume fractions across 3 problem types; 6-7 values per table (Tables 1-7)

notes: The abstract's principal comparison is design quality, so coded in quality stratum. The manuscript supplies CNN code in Appendix A, but does not establish that the complete benchmark/data pipeline is runnable under a stated license.
